Profit then carries interest at SOFR plus spread and margin on the loan less 15,882 from the swap, which is 1.7910 percent plus spread and margin on the hedged 479,970, the fixed rate the hedge was meant to deliver. A reserve loss that is not expected to be recovered is reclassified at once (para. 6.5.11(d)(iii)). If hedge accounting stops, the reserve stays while the cash flows are still expected, and goes straight to profit if they no longer are (para. 6.5.12).

6. Equity investments at FVOCI

An equity investment that is not held for trading may be designated, irrevocably and share by share, at FVOCI (PSAK 109.5.7.5). The lecture notes call these "non-trading" equity investments, held, for example, to secure supply of a raw material.

The difference from debt at FVOCI is that nothing is ever recycled. Dividends go to profit or loss unless they clearly recover part of the cost, there is no impairment test, and on sale the cumulative gain or loss may only be transferred within equity (para. B5.7.1). PHE's policy elects FVOCI for its non-listed equity investments (Note 3g(i), Daftar 5/40–5/41, PDF pp. 57–58). Note 16 shows "other investments" of 63 without a measurement basis (Daftar 5/107, PDF p. 124).

For example (illustration), a stake bought for 1,000 is worth 1,400 at year end, pays a dividend of 50, and is sold the next year for 1,400.

7. Revaluation surplus and remeasurements: never recycled

Two more OCI items never return to profit. Under the revaluation model of PSAK 216 Property, Plant and Equipment (formerly PSAK 16, IAS 16), an increase goes to OCI as revaluation surplus, and a decrease is charged first against the surplus held for that asset and only the excess to profit (paras. 39–40). The surplus may be transferred to retained earnings as the asset is used or derecognised (para. 41). The Fixed Assets essay teaches the model.

For example (illustration), a building carried at 2,000 with 20 years left is revalued to 2,600. A year later its fair value is 1,800.

Surplus = 2,600 − 2,000 = 600: Dr Building 600 / Cr OCI, revaluation surplus 600

Depreciation = 2,600 / 20 = 130 against 2,000 / 20 = 100 on the old amount; transfer = 130 − 100 = 30: Dr Revaluation surplus 30 / Cr Retained earnings 30

Carrying amount = 2,600 − 130 = 2,470; decrease = 2,470 − 1,800 = 670

Surplus left = 600 − 30 = 570, so Dr OCI, revaluation surplus 570, Dr Revaluation loss 100 / Cr Building 670

Remeasurements of a defined benefit plan go to OCI and are never reclassified (PSAK 219.122). PHE's −610 is that item; the Employee Benefits essay teaches it. Actuarial gains and losses on other long-term benefits, such as PHE's long-service awards, skip OCI and are "charged immediately to profit or loss" (Note 3q(iv), Daftar 5/65, PDF p. 82).

8. Tax on OCI items

Tax follows the item. Tax on an item recognised in OCI is recognised in OCI (PSAK 212.61A, formerly PSAK 46, IAS 12), as PHE's policy says (Note 3s, Daftar 5/67, PDF p. 84). Each OCI item may be presented net of tax, or before tax with one tax line allocated between the two groups (PSAK 201.91). PHE presents the hedge line "net of tax".

For example (illustration), Case A's hedge loss of 11,000 in OCI before tax, at an illustrative tax rate of 40 percent, reduces a future taxable gain, so it creates a deferred tax asset.

Deferred tax = 11,000 × 40% = 4,400; OCI net of tax = 11,000 − 4,400 = 6,600

Dr Deferred tax asset 4,400 / Cr OCI, tax on cash flow hedge 4,400

The same applies to revaluation surpluses and remeasurements, but a subsidiary's translation differences usually carry no deferred tax, because a parent that controls the timing of reversal and does not expect it soon recognises none (PSAK 212.39; see the Deferred Tax essay).

9. OCI across industries

Banks. Banks hold large government bond portfolios, many in a hold-to-collect-and-sell business model and so at FVOCI. When yields rise, equity falls through OCI before any bond is sold, and a sale for liquidity recycles the reserve.

Insurers. Under PSAK 117 Insurance Contracts (formerly PSAK 74, IFRS 17), effective for Indonesian insurers from 1 January 2025, an insurer may split insurance finance income or expense between profit and OCI (IFRS 17.88). With its bonds at FVOCI, interest-rate swings on both sides of the balance sheet then meet in OCI.

Utilities and property. Revaluation surpluses dominate OCI where the revaluation model is used, such as PLN's 2015 revaluation (see the Fixed Assets essay). The surplus never recycles, so the higher depreciation lowers profit while the surplus moves to retained earnings in step.

Islamic finance. A sukuk investor classifies its holding under PSAK 410 Akuntansi Sukuk (formerly PSAK 110), whose 2015 revision added an FVOCI category for sukuk held to collect and sell, so OCI works as it does for conventional debt in section 2.

Associates. An investor's share of an associate's OCI is presented in its own OCI, split into the two groups (PSAK 201.82A; see the Long-term Investments essay). PHE has no such line (see Least-confident).

NCI share of OCI = 8,487 / 37,360 = 22.7%

Hedges are 58.7 percent of the year's OCI and translation 39.6 percent. NCI absorbed 22.7 percent of OCI against 3.8 percent of profit (119,560 / 3,121,035). PHE's dollar-priced PSC entities produce no translation differences, so the translation line comes from Elnusa, its only rupiah-functional subsidiary, 48.90 percent outside-owned.

NCI share of translation loss = 48.90% × 14,810 = 7,242, about 85% of NCI's OCI loss of 8,487

The other 1,245 is unexplained, since PHE does not attribute OCI by subsidiary; the hedge sits in 99-percent-owned PEPC and the whole remeasurement line is only −610.

Note 14b carries the hedge as an unrealised gain of 50,769 (2023: 66,533) in other non-current assets (Daftar 5/105, PDF p. 122; see the Advances and Prepayments essay). PHE gives no reconciliation of the hedge reserve or of reclassification adjustments, which PSAK 107 asks for (IFRS 7.24E).

11. Related lines

  • oci-translation-adjustments: the translation line, section 4.

  • oci-cash-flow-hedge: the hedge line, section 5.

  • oci-remeasurement-employee-benefits: the remeasurement line, taught in the Employee Benefits essay.

  • other-non-current-assets: holds the unrealised hedge gain of 50,769.

  • long-term-bank-loans-non-current: the JTB loan behind the hedge.

  • non-controlling-interest: carries NCI's share of OCI.

  • retained-earnings: receives transfers of non-recycled reserves.

  • deferred-tax-assets, deferred-tax-liabilities: tax on OCI items.

Least-confident assertions

  • Elnusa's translation explains about 7,242 of NCI's OCI loss of 8,487; the other 1,245 is unexplained, and in 2023 NCI's OCI fell (−2,008) while translation rose (+2,595), so more than Elnusa drives it. The closing rates are implied from Note 48 (Note 3r prints both years as USD 0.06 per Rp1,000).

  • The hedge figures do not reconcile. A settlement received lowers the swap asset and leaves OCI by the same amount, so pre-tax hedge OCI should move with the asset (−15,764, give or take the 1,395 of ineffectiveness), yet the line is −21,940 after tax. Note 14b puts the 1,395 "included in finance costs", but Note 41 has no row for it; Note 40 shows an "adjustment of hedging portion" of 173 in finance income for 2023 and nil for 2024 (Daftar 5/150, PDF p. 167), so the 2024 amount is probably inside interest expense from loans. The swaps' amortisation profile is not disclosed, so section 5's cases are illustrations.

  • Note 43e's OCI column (Daftar 5/155, PDF p. 172) holds −6 and +167 against employee benefits, +310 against "others" and −1,689 against the inventory provision, which may be translation of a rupiah subsidiary's balances. There is no hedge row, so the tax implied by "net of tax" cannot be located.

  • Note 16b shows "other changes" in associates of −59,610 (Daftar 5/108, PDF p. 125), but PHE's OCI has no line for the share of associates' OCI (PSAK 201.82A(b)). Whether these changes are OCI, distributions or something else is not disclosed.

  • PHE's policy for listed equity at FVTPL differs between languages (Note 3g(i), Daftar 5/41, PDF p. 58). The Indonesian omits "tidak" ("yang mana oleh Grup diklasifikasikan secara takterbatalkan pada NWPKL") and so reads as the opposite of the English "had not irrevocably elected"; this essay follows the English. The policy also lists quoted FVOCI debt (PDF p. 57), yet OCI has no FVOCI line.

content.text: Other comprehensive income (OCI) holds gains and losses on remeasuring assets and liabilities that the standards keep out of profit or loss, because putting them there would make profit a worse guide to performance. Profit plus OCI is comprehensive income, every change in equity in the period except transactions with owners and retrospective adjustments.

Each OCI item is either recycled or not. Translation differences on foreign operations, cash flow hedge results and fair value changes on debt investments at FVOCI later leave OCI, mostly by reclassification to profit or loss. Revaluation surpluses, remeasurements of defined benefit plans and fair value changes on equity investments at FVOCI never are, though they may be moved within equity to retained earnings.

When an item is recycled, the reclassification adjustment takes it out of OCI in the same period it enters profit or loss, so comprehensive income counts it once. The tax on each item follows it into OCI.

PT Pertamina Hulu Energi and subsidiaries (PHE) report accumulated other comprehensive income of 103,851 at 31 December 2024 against 132,724 a year earlier, in USD thousand (PHE FS 2024, statement of financial position, Daftar 1/3, PDF p. 13; "Daftar" is the printed page). The balance is 0.69 percent of total equity of 15,107,352 (0.94 percent a year earlier). The flow behind it is in the statement of profit or loss and other comprehensive income: translation adjustments of −14,810 (2023: 2,595), cash flow hedges, net of tax, of −21,940 (2023: −2,649), and a remeasurement of the employee benefit liability of −610 (2023: 1,430), a total of −37,360 (Daftar 2/1, PDF p. 14).

After reading it a student should be able to say why an item goes to OCI, record translation, hedge, FVOCI and revaluation entries, and follow an amount into accumulated OCI and, where required, back to profit or loss.
All amounts are in USD thousand unless stated. Figures from PHE's statements are cited to their note. Every other number is labelled an illustration.

OCI exists because some changes in the value of assets and liabilities say little about how the period went. The lecture notes on Kieso's chapter 4 open with the income statement's purpose, to evaluate past performance and predict future performance. A gain that comes only from the rupiah weakening, or from rates moving a ten-year swap, makes that prediction harder, yet leaving such changes off the balance sheet would carry assets and liabilities at stale amounts.
The standards resolve this with a second section of the performance statement. The 2018 Conceptual Framework (in Indonesia the KKPK,

) makes profit or loss the primary source of information about performance and lets the IASB, standard by standard and only in exceptional circumstances, send a change in the current value of an asset or liability to OCI where that makes profit more relevant or more faithful (paras. 7.15–7.17). It presumes that OCI is recycled later when that improves profit for that period (para. 7.19). No general principle selects the items.
The two sections add up to

, the change in equity from everything except transactions with owners in their capacity as owners (PSAK 201.7, formerly PSAK 1, IAS 1). If every non-owner change in equity passes through one statement, nothing reaches equity unreported, apart from retrospective corrections of opening balances (PSAK 208) and transfers between components. PHE's 2024 figures show the identity.
Profit for the year 3,121,035 + OCI (−14,810 − 21,940 − 610) = 3,121,035 − 37,360 = 3,083,675 total comprehensive income
2. Presenting OCI: the two groups and reclassification adjustments

An entity presents profit or loss and OCI either in one statement with two sections or in two statements, the second starting from profit (PSAK 201.10A), as the lecture notes on chapter 17 set out. PHE uses one statement (Daftar 2/1–2/2, PDF pp. 14–15). Within the OCI section the items are grouped by what will happen to them later (PSAK 201.82A):
Will not be reclassified to profit or loss
May be reclassified to profit or loss
Revaluation surplus on fixed assets and intangibles (PSAK 216, PSAK 238)
Effective portion of cash flow hedges and net investment hedges, and the cost of hedging (PSAK 109)
Fair value changes on equity investments designated at FVOCI (PSAK 109)
Fair value changes on debt investments at FVOCI (PSAK 109)
Own-credit changes on liabilities designated at fair value (PSAK 109)
Insurance finance income or expense, where the OCI option is taken (PSAK 117)
Share of associates' and joint ventures' OCI that will not be reclassified
Share of associates' and joint ventures' OCI that may be reclassified

A loss in the right-hand column is one that profit will see later; one on the left never reaches profit. OCI is also attributed between owners of the parent and non-controlling interests (para. 81B), because a subsidiary's OCI belongs partly to its outside shareholders. From 1 January 2027 PSAK 118 (IFRS 18) replaces PSAK 201; it keeps the OCI section and its two groups and changes mainly the profit-or-loss section above it.
When a recycled item is realised, its gain or loss enters profit, but it was already counted in comprehensive income when it went to OCI, so it must leave OCI in the same period. That deduction is a

(paras. 7, 92–93). The lecture notes on Kieso's chapter 17 introduce it with debt investments held to collect and sell, measured at fair value through OCI (FVOCI). Interest at the effective rate, expected credit losses and exchange differences go to profit, the remaining fair value change to OCI, and on derecognition the cumulative OCI goes to profit (PSAK 109.4.1.2A, 5.7.10–5.7.11).

For example (illustration), a PHE subsidiary buys US dollar bonds at par for 10,000 on 1 January 2024, coupon 5 percent paid annually, held to collect and sell. At the end of 2024 their fair value is 10,400. On 31 December 2025, after the second coupon, it sells them for 10,250.
2024: Dr Debt investment 400 / Cr OCI, fair value change 400
2025, to fair value at sale: Dr OCI, fair value change 150 / Cr Debt investment 150
Sale: Dr Cash 10,250 / Cr Debt investment 10,250
Reclassification: Dr OCI, reclassification adjustment 250 / Cr Gain on sale of debt investment 250

Over two years comprehensive income is 1,250, the coupons of 1,000 plus 250 of gain over cost. Without the reclassification adjustment the total would be 1,500, with the 250 counted in 2024's OCI and again in 2025's profit.

The lecture notes need three corrections here. Their recycling example for "perusahaan Ali" reads "Fair value of portofilio : $34.000 / Less cost of portofolio : $34.000 / Unrealized gain : $4.000"; the cost must be 30,000. Their Saratoga sale states a price of "$95.000.000" but debits cash of $98,500,000, and its entry ("Cash $98.500.000 / Debt Investment $98.185.648,32 / Gain on sale of debt investment $314.351,68") removes only the amortised cost, leaving both the fair value adjustment and the unrealised holding gain on the books. Under PSAK 109 the asset leaves at fair value and the gain is reclassified at the sale, as in the last journal above. And their FVOCI impairment example follows an incurred-loss model; under PSAK 109 the expected credit loss on FVOCI debt is charged to profit with the other side in OCI, so the asset stays at fair value (para. 5.5.2).
What passes through OCI collects in equity as

, one of the components of equity in the lecture notes on Kieso's chapter 15. As those notes put it, the statement of changes in equity reconciles each component from opening to closing, with OCI analysed by item there or in the notes (PSAK 201.106–106A). Groups often keep one reserve per kind (translation, cash flow hedge, fair value, revaluation surplus), because the components leave equity by different routes: reclassification to profit or loss, transfer within equity to retained earnings for items never recycled, or, for hedges of non-financial items, removal into the asset's carrying amount.
PHE keeps one column for all of it. Its statement of changes in equity moves accumulated OCI from 132,724 to 103,851 by the owners' share of the year's OCI and nothing else (Daftar 3, PDF p. 16).
Owners' share of OCI = total comprehensive income to owners 2,972,602 − profit to owners 3,001,475 = −28,873
Translation differences arise because a group reports in one currency and some of its members keep their books in another. PSAK 221
The Effects of Changes in Foreign Exchange Rates
, that of the primary economic environment that mainly drives an entity's prices and costs, from the

the statements are presented in. Foreign-currency monetary items are retranslated into the functional currency through profit or loss (see the Foreign Exchange Loss essay; PHE's foreign exchange loss, net, of 4,479 in 2024 is of this kind). Translation into another presentation currency is a separate step.

PHE's functional currency is the US dollar for every entity except Elnusa, whose functional currency is the rupiah, and the consolidated statements are presented in dollars (Note 3a and 3r, Daftar 5/29 and 5/66, PDF pp. 46 and 83). Elnusa's statements are translated as PSAK 221.39 requires, and PHE's policy restates it (Note 3r(iii), Daftar 5/67, PDF p. 84): assets and liabilities at the closing JISDOR rate, income and expenses at average rates, and "all of the resulting exchange differences are recognized in other comprehensive income".
Why the difference goes to OCI.

It arises from translating opening net assets at a new closing rate and profit at average rates (para. 41). Neither changes Elnusa's rupiah cash flows, and nothing is realised until the parent sells, so the difference stays out of profit until disposal.

For example (illustration), take Elnusa's net assets in rupiah as Rp5,000,000 million at the start of 2024, about half its total assets before elimination of 621,898 (Note 1b), and its profit as Rp500,000 million, with no dividends. The closing rates implied by PHE's Note 48 are Rp15,439 per dollar for 2023 (6,377,542 / 413.080, trade payables) and Rp16,157 for 2024 (8,369,504 / 518.011) (Daftar 5/225, PDF p. 242). Assume an average rate for 2024 of Rp15,850.

The rupiah lost 4.44 percent against the dollar (1 − 15,439 / 16,157), so the subsidiary is worth fewer dollars. PHE owns 51.10 percent of Elnusa (Note 1b, Daftar 5/6, PDF p. 23), so 48.90 percent of the difference belongs to non-controlling interests (para. 41).
Dr OCI, translation adjustments 14,991 / Cr Net assets of Elnusa (translated) 14,991, attributed as 7,660 to the owners' translation reserve and 7,331 to NCI

When the foreign operation is disposed of, the owners' cumulative translation difference is reclassified to profit or loss as part of the gain or loss on disposal (para. 48). Losing control counts as a disposal even if an interest is kept (para. 48A). The NCI's share is derecognised with the NCI and never recycled (para. 48B). If PHE sold all of Elnusa and the owners' reserve for it held −7,660, that loss would leave equity with the sale.
Dr Loss on disposal of subsidiary 7,660 / Cr Translation reserve 7,660
A partial sale that keeps control is a transaction with owners. The proportionate share of the reserve is re-attributed to NCI, not recycled (para. 48C; see the Non-controlling Interest essay).

Hedge accounting exists to fix a timing mismatch. A derivative is measured at fair value through profit or loss (PSAK 109.4.1.4), while the hedged risk may be a cash flow that does not exist yet, such as next year's floating-rate interest, so the swap's value would swing through profit years before the interest it fixes. PSAK 109 offers three relationships (para. 6.5.2), all restated in PHE's policy (Note 3g(iv), Daftar 5/47–5/51, PDF pp. 64–68): a
, where both sides go to profit; a
of variable cash flows from a recognised item or a highly probable forecast transaction; and a
in a foreign operation, accounted for like a cash flow hedge.

The relationship must be designated and documented at inception and meet three effectiveness requirements: an economic relationship between hedged item and hedging instrument, credit risk not dominating the value changes, and a hedge ratio equal to the one actually used (para. 6.4.1).
For a cash flow hedge the

is set at the lower, in absolute amounts, of the cumulative gain or loss on the instrument and the cumulative change in value of the hedged cash flows since inception. The part of the instrument's result that fits inside that limit is the effective portion and goes to OCI; the rest is ineffectiveness and goes to profit or loss (para. 6.5.11(a)–(c)). The hedged item's change is usually measured with a
, a perfect swap on the hedged cash flows.

PHE's subsidiary PT Pertamina EP Cepu (PEPC, 99 percent owned) borrowed for the Jambaran–Tiung Biru (JTB) gas project at SOFR plus a credit adjustment spread and margin, with 1,208,418 outstanding at the end of 2024 (Note 27, Daftar 5/132, PDF p. 149). It has swapped the loan to fixed rates of 1.7910 to 1.9866 percent on notionals of 839,970 at the effective dates, the largest being Conventional Tranche B, 479,970 at 1.7910 percent to March 2029 (Note 27, Daftar 5/133, PDF p. 150), and accounts for the swaps as cash flow hedges (Note 14b, Daftar 5/106, PDF p. 123). With SOFR far above those rates the swaps are an asset, the unrealised hedge gain of 50,769 (2023: 66,533) in other non-current assets. When markets expect rate cuts, the fixed rate is worth less and the asset falls. For example (illustration), measure from a designation at the start of 2024, so that the year's change is the cumulative change.
Cumulative fall in the swap's value
Cumulative change in hedged cash flows (hypothetical derivative)
Cash flow hedge reserve (lower of the two)
Dr OCI, cash flow hedge 11,000, Dr Finance cost 1,000 / Cr Derivative asset 12,000
Dr OCI, cash flow hedge 10,000 / Cr Derivative asset 10,000
The cap keeps OCI within what the hedged cash flows can absorb; Case B shows an under-hedge is not charged to profit.

If the hedged transaction produces a non-financial asset or liability, such as equipment bought in euros under a forward, the reserve goes into the asset's initial cost as a basis adjustment. Otherwise, as for PEPC's interest, it is reclassified to profit or loss when the hedged cash flows affect profit (para. 6.5.11(d)). Suppose (illustration) SOFR averages 5.10 percent over a year and the swap settles net on Tranche B's original notional (the amortisation profile is not disclosed).
Dr OCI, reclassification adjustment 15,882 / Cr Finance cost 15,882

Profit then carries interest at SOFR plus spread and margin on the loan less 15,882 from the swap, which is 1.7910 percent plus spread and margin on the hedged 479,970, the fixed rate the hedge was meant to deliver. A reserve loss that is not expected to be recovered is reclassified at once (para. 6.5.11(d)(iii)). If hedge accounting stops, the reserve stays while the cash flows are still expected, and goes straight to profit if they no longer are (para. 6.5.12).

An equity investment that is not held for trading may be designated, irrevocably and share by share, at FVOCI (PSAK 109.5.7.5). The lecture notes call these "non-trading" equity investments, held, for example, to secure supply of a raw material.

The difference from debt at FVOCI is that nothing is ever recycled. Dividends go to profit or loss unless they clearly recover part of the cost, there is no impairment test, and on sale the cumulative gain or loss may only be transferred within equity (para. B5.7.1). PHE's policy elects FVOCI for its non-listed equity investments (Note 3g(i), Daftar 5/40–5/41, PDF pp. 57–58). Note 16 shows "other investments" of 63 without a measurement basis (Daftar 5/107, PDF p. 124).
For example (illustration), a stake bought for 1,000 is worth 1,400 at year end, pays a dividend of 50, and is sold the next year for 1,400.
Dr Equity investment 400 / Cr OCI, fair value reserve 400
Dr Equity investment 400 / Cr Gain on investment 400
Dr Cash 1,400 / Cr Equity investment 1,400; Dr Fair value reserve 400 / Cr Retained earnings 400
Equity ends the same under both, but FVOCI profit never shows the 400, so a sale cannot be timed to lift profit.
7. Revaluation surplus and remeasurements: never recycled
Two more OCI items never return to profit. Under the revaluation model of PSAK 216
(formerly PSAK 16, IAS 16), an increase goes to OCI as

, and a decrease is charged first against the surplus held for that asset and only the excess to profit (paras. 39–40). The surplus may be transferred to retained earnings as the asset is used or derecognised (para. 41). The Fixed Assets essay teaches the model.
For example (illustration), a building carried at 2,000 with 20 years left is revalued to 2,600. A year later its fair value is 1,800.
Surplus = 2,600 − 2,000 = 600: Dr Building 600 / Cr OCI, revaluation surplus 600
Depreciation = 2,600 / 20 = 130 against 2,000 / 20 = 100 on the old amount; transfer = 130 − 100 = 30: Dr Revaluation surplus 30 / Cr Retained earnings 30
Surplus left = 600 − 30 = 570, so Dr OCI, revaluation surplus 570, Dr Revaluation loss 100 / Cr Building 670

Remeasurements of a defined benefit plan go to OCI and are never reclassified (PSAK 219.122). PHE's −610 is that item; the Employee Benefits essay teaches it. Actuarial gains and losses on other long-term benefits, such as PHE's long-service awards, skip OCI and are "charged immediately to profit or loss" (Note 3q(iv), Daftar 5/65, PDF p. 82).

Tax follows the item. Tax on an item recognised in OCI is recognised in OCI (PSAK 212.61A, formerly PSAK 46, IAS 12), as PHE's policy says (Note 3s, Daftar 5/67, PDF p. 84). Each OCI item may be presented net of tax, or before tax with one tax line allocated between the two groups (PSAK 201.91). PHE presents the hedge line "net of tax".
For example (illustration), Case A's hedge loss of 11,000 in OCI before tax, at an illustrative tax rate of 40 percent, reduces a future taxable gain, so it creates a deferred tax asset.
Dr Deferred tax asset 4,400 / Cr OCI, tax on cash flow hedge 4,400

The same applies to revaluation surpluses and remeasurements, but a subsidiary's translation differences usually carry no deferred tax, because a parent that controls the timing of reversal and does not expect it soon recognises none (PSAK 212.39; see the Deferred Tax essay).

Banks hold large government bond portfolios, many in a hold-to-collect-and-sell business model and so at FVOCI. When yields rise, equity falls through OCI before any bond is sold, and a sale for liquidity recycles the reserve.

(formerly PSAK 74, IFRS 17), effective for Indonesian insurers from 1 January 2025, an insurer may split insurance finance income or expense between profit and OCI (IFRS 17.88). With its bonds at FVOCI, interest-rate swings on both sides of the balance sheet then meet in OCI.

Revaluation surpluses dominate OCI where the revaluation model is used, such as PLN's 2015 revaluation (see the Fixed Assets essay). The surplus never recycles, so the higher depreciation lowers profit while the surplus moves to retained earnings in step.
A sukuk investor classifies its holding under PSAK 410
(formerly PSAK 110), whose 2015 revision added an FVOCI category for sukuk held to collect and sell, so OCI works as it does for conventional debt in section 2.
An investor's share of an associate's OCI is presented in its own OCI, split into the two groups (PSAK 201.82A; see the Long-term Investments essay). PHE has no such line (see Least-confident).
PHE shows the OCI section on the face of the statement, without a note of its own (Daftar 2/1–2/2, PDF pp. 14–15; Daftar 3, PDF p. 16).
Cash flow hedges, net of tax (may be reclassified)
Remeasurement of employee benefit liability (not reclassified)
Attributable to owners of the parent
Accumulated OCI, owners, at year end

Hedges are 58.7 percent of the year's OCI and translation 39.6 percent. NCI absorbed 22.7 percent of OCI against 3.8 percent of profit (119,560 / 3,121,035). PHE's dollar-priced PSC entities produce no translation differences, so the translation line comes from Elnusa, its only rupiah-functional subsidiary, 48.90 percent outside-owned.
NCI share of translation loss = 48.90% × 14,810 = 7,242, about 85% of NCI's OCI loss of 8,487
The other 1,245 is unexplained, since PHE does not attribute OCI by subsidiary; the hedge sits in 99-percent-owned PEPC and the whole remeasurement line is only −610.

Note 14b carries the hedge as an unrealised gain of 50,769 (2023: 66,533) in other non-current assets (Daftar 5/105, PDF p. 122; see the Advances and Prepayments essay). PHE gives no reconciliation of the hedge reserve or of reclassification adjustments, which PSAK 107 asks for (IFRS 7.24E).
: the remeasurement line, taught in the Employee Benefits essay.
: holds the unrealised hedge gain of 50,769.
: the JTB loan behind the hedge.

Elnusa's translation explains about 7,242 of NCI's OCI loss of 8,487; the other 1,245 is unexplained, and in 2023 NCI's OCI fell (−2,008) while translation rose (+2,595), so more than Elnusa drives it. The closing rates are implied from Note 48 (Note 3r prints both years as USD 0.06 per Rp1,000).

The hedge figures do not reconcile. A settlement received lowers the swap asset and leaves OCI by the same amount, so pre-tax hedge OCI should move with the asset (−15,764, give or take the 1,395 of ineffectiveness), yet the line is −21,940 after tax. Note 14b puts the 1,395 "included in finance costs", but Note 41 has no row for it; Note 40 shows an "adjustment of hedging portion" of 173 in finance income for 2023 and nil for 2024 (Daftar 5/150, PDF p. 167), so the 2024 amount is probably inside interest expense from loans. The swaps' amortisation profile is not disclosed, so section 5's cases are illustrations.

presentation.deck: The theory of other comprehensive income from its purpose to recycling, worked through PHE's translation and hedge reserves and set beside the industries where OCI moves equity most
key_takeaways: Other comprehensive income (OCI) holds gains and losses on remeasuring assets and liabilities that the standards keep out of profit or loss, because putting them there would make profit a worse guide to performance. Profit plus OCI is comprehensive income, every change in equity in the period except transactions with owners and retrospective adjustments.

Each OCI item is either recycled or not. Translation differences on foreign operations, cash flow hedge results and fair value changes on debt investments at FVOCI later leave OCI, mostly by reclassification to profit or loss. Revaluation surpluses, remeasurements of defined benefit plans and fair value changes on equity investments at FVOCI never are, though they may be moved within equity to retained earnings.

When an item is recycled, the reclassification adjustment takes it out of OCI in the same period it enters profit or loss, so comprehensive income counts it once. The tax on each item follows it into OCI.

title: Other Taxes Receivable: VAT, Withholding and the Taxes Outside PSAK 212
snippet: The theory of indirect and withheld taxes from the VAT invoice to the Tax Court, worked through PHE's reimbursable VAT and set beside the industries with their own rules
content:
In brief

  • Taxes other than income tax fall outside PSAK 212. For each one, the accounting depends on who bears the tax. Tax the entity collects or withholds for the state is a liability. Tax it pays and can recover is a receivable. Tax it pays and cannot recover is part of the cost of what it bought.

  • Value added tax (VAT) is collected at every stage of a supply chain, and each business pays the state only output VAT less input VAT. When input exceeds output, the business is owed money. It carries the excess forward or claims a refund, and exporters and suppliers to VAT collectors are owed money most months.

  • An upstream oil and gas contractor sells crude and piped gas whose supply is exempt from VAT, so it cannot credit its input VAT. Under its production sharing contract (PSC) the government reimburses that VAT out of the state's share of production. At PHE, reimbursable VAT is 505,861 of the 563,451 other taxes receivable at the end of 2024, 475,338 of it in the subsidiaries that hold the PSCs.

PT Pertamina Hulu Energi and subsidiaries (PHE) report other taxes receivable, current portion, of 300,738 at 31 December 2024 against 275,612 a year earlier, and a non-current portion of 262,713 against 213,492, in USD thousand (PHE FS 2024, statement of financial position, Daftar 1/1, PDF p. 11; Note 43a, Daftar 5/151, PDF p. 168; "Daftar" is the printed page). The current portion is 0.99 percent of total assets and 3.74 percent of current assets (0.89 and 2.79 percent a year earlier); the two portions together, 563,451, are 1.85 percent of total assets. On the other side PHE owes other taxes of 153,068 against 152,476 (Note 43b, Daftar 5/152, PDF p. 169). This page covers all three lines.

After reading it a student should be able to say who bears each tax, record VAT and withholding from invoice to settlement, measure a disputed or reimbursable claim, and classify it between current and non-current.

All amounts are in USD thousand unless stated. Figures from PHE's statements are cited to their note. Every other number is labelled an illustration.

1. Which taxes are "other" taxes

PSAK 212 Income Taxes (formerly PSAK 46, IAS 12) covers taxes based on taxable profit, including taxes withheld on distributions to the entity (para. 2). Everything else is an "other" tax, such as VAT, taxes the entity withholds from other people's income, land and building tax (Pajak Bumi dan Bangunan, PBB), import duties and regional taxes. Corporate income tax receivable and payable, current and deferred, belong to the Corporate and Dividend Taxes Receivable and Deferred Tax essays.

No single standard covers other taxes. The accounting comes from asking who bears the tax, and the answer puts the entity in one of three roles.

Role

Example

What the entity records

Collector or agent: the tax belongs to someone else

VAT on its own sales; income tax withheld from employees and suppliers

a liability until it pays the state

Taxpayer who can recover the tax

input VAT creditable against output VAT; VAT reimbursed under a PSC

a receivable

Taxpayer who bears the tax

input VAT that cannot be credited; PBB; non-recoverable import duties

an expense, or part of an asset's cost

The third row is already written into the asset standards. Inventory cost includes taxes "other than those subsequently recoverable" from the tax authority (PSAK 202.11, formerly PSAK 14, IAS 2), and a fixed asset's cost includes non-refundable purchase taxes (PSAK 216.16(a), formerly PSAK 16, IAS 16).

2. Sales tax and VAT: the collector's liability

A state that wants to tax consumption cannot collect from millions of consumers, so it makes businesses collect for it. The lecture notes, following Kieso's chapter on current liabilities, distinguish a tax on every sale from a tax on value added only. In its usual form a sales tax is charged once, at the retail sale to the consumer. A value added tax is charged at every sale along the chain, and each business deducts the tax it paid on its purchases, so each pays the state tax only on the value it added.

For example (illustration), at the 2024 Indonesian VAT rate of 11 percent, a chemical maker sells to a distributor for 400, the distributor sells to a retailer for 700, and the retailer sells to a consumer for 1,000.

Maker: output VAT = 400 × 11% = 44; pays 44

Distributor: output VAT = 700 × 11% = 77; input VAT 44; pays 33

Retailer: output VAT = 1,000 × 11% = 110; input VAT 77; pays 33

Total paid = 44 + 33 + 33 = 110 = 1,000 × 11%

VAT reaches the retail sales tax's total in three payments of 11 percent of each stage's value added (400, 300 and 300). If the retailer evades, the state has still received 77 of the 110.

The retailer's entries, side by side, in the format of the lecture notes:

Sales tax

VAT

Purchase of 700

Dr Inventories 700 / Cr Cash 700

Dr Inventories 700, Dr VAT input 77 / Cr Cash 777

Sale of 1,000

Dr Cash 1,110 / Cr Sales revenue 1,000, Cr Sales tax payable 110

Dr Cash 1,110 / Cr Sales revenue 1,000, Cr VAT output 110

Month end

(none)

Dr VAT output 110 / Cr VAT input 77, Cr VAT payable 33

Payment to the state

Dr Sales tax payable 110 / Cr Cash 110

Dr VAT payable 33 / Cr Cash 33

Revenue is 1,000 in both columns, because amounts collected for third parties, such as sales taxes, are not part of the transaction price (PSAK 115.47, formerly PSAK 72, IFRS 15). When a till records only the tax-inclusive total, revenue is backed out of it.

Revenue = 1,110 / 1.11 = 1,000; VAT = 1,110 − 1,000 = 110

From 2025 the rate is 12 percent, but on a base of 11/12 of the price for non-luxury goods, so the effective rate stays 11 percent (PMK 131/2024).

3. Input VAT, crediting and overpayment

A VAT-registered business (Pengusaha Kena Pajak, PKP) settles VAT by tax period, which in Indonesia is a month. Within each month it credits input VAT against output VAT (UU PPN art. 9). A positive balance is paid to the state. A negative one is an overpayment, and the general rule carries it forward to the next month as a credit (kompensasi), and a cash refund (restitusi) can be requested only at the end of the financial year (art. 9(4) and (4a)). Some businesses may request a refund every month (art. 9(4b)), among them exporters and those whose sales go to VAT collectors (section 4).

For example (illustration), a chemicals distributor selling to manufacturers records three months.

January

February

March

Output VAT

500

300

450

Input VAT

380

520

200

Net for the month

120 payable

220 overpaid

250 payable

Credit brought forward

(220)

Paid to the state

120

0

30

January: Dr VAT output 500 / Cr VAT input 380, Cr VAT payable 120

February: Dr VAT output 300, Dr VAT overpaid, carried forward 220 / Cr VAT input 520

March: Dr VAT output 450 / Cr VAT input 200, Cr VAT overpaid, carried forward 220, Cr VAT payable 30

The 220 at the end of February is a receivable, recovered by paying 220 less in March. At year end a refund request would start a tax examination (see the Corporate and Dividend Taxes Receivable essay).

4. When input VAT cannot be credited, and VAT collectors

Non-creditable input VAT is cost. Crediting needs output VAT to credit against. A business whose own supplies are not subject to VAT has none, so the input VAT it pays is a cost like any other part of the price (section 1, third row). PHE's policy, in its Indonesian text, puts VAT that "tidak dapat dikreditkan" (cannot be credited) into the cost of the asset or the expense, and carries the net VAT claimed for refund, or owed, as an asset or liability (Note 3s, Daftar 5/70, PDF p. 87). It does not mention reimbursement (section 10). For example (illustration), a company with only exempt supplies buys casing for 1,000 plus VAT of 110.

Dr Inventories 1,110 / Cr Trade payables 1,110

VAT collectors. Some buyers are appointed pemungut PPN, VAT collectors. The supplier still charges VAT and issues a tax invoice, but the buyer withholds the VAT from its payment and pays it to the state itself. Upstream oil and gas contractors and geothermal contractors are such collectors, for purchases above Rp10 million (full amount) including tax (PMK 81/2024, arts. 298–299).

For example (illustration), a contractor buys 2,000 of well services, VAT 2,000 × 11% = 220. For simplicity the buyer books the collected VAT when the invoice arrives, although it collects it on payment.

Buyer (VAT collector)

Supplier

Dr Production expenses 2,000, Dr VAT input 220 / Cr Trade payables 2,000, Cr VAT collected, payable 220

Dr Trade receivables 2,220 / Cr Revenue 2,000, Cr VAT output 220

Dr Trade payables 2,000 / Cr Cash 2,000

Dr Cash 2,000, Dr VAT output 220 / Cr Trade receivables 2,220

Dr VAT collected, payable 220 / Cr Cash 220

The buyer settles the supplier's output VAT, so the supplier has nothing left to credit its own input VAT against. If it paid 130 of input VAT that month, it is overpaid by 130, and next month again, which is why art. 9(4b) lets it claim every month.

5. Upstream: VAT reimbursement under a PSC

An upstream contractor pays VAT on almost everything it buys and charges VAT on almost nothing it sells. Until March 2022, mining and drilling output taken directly from its source was outside VAT (UU PPN art. 4A(2)(a)). The Job Creation Law took coal out of that exclusion in November 2020, and the Harmonised Tax Law (UU 7/2021) deleted the exclusion altogether. Crude oil, piped natural gas and geothermal steam are now taxable goods whose supply is exempt (PP 49/2022, art. 6(2)). Input VAT on exempt supplies cannot be credited (art. 16B(3)), so under section 4's rule it would be a cost.

The PSC changes that. An operating contractor may claim reimbursement of the VAT it has paid on goods and services for its working area, where its contract provides for it. The rules were PMK 218/PMK.02/2014, replaced in August 2019 by PMK 119/PMK.02/2019, which was in turn replaced on 31 December 2024, PHE's balance-sheet date, by PMK 139/2024. The claim goes to SKK Migas, the upstream regulator, which verifies the tax payments with the Directorate General of Taxes (DJP), and the Ministry of Finance pays it from the oil and gas account at Bank Indonesia. Under the 2014 and 2019 texts, three limits decide how much comes back and when.

  1. VAT that was exempt, VAT on LNG plant operating costs, and VAT on procurement that cannot be charged to operating costs are excluded (2014, art. 3(2)).

  2. Reimbursement is paid only after the state's share of production from the working area has been received.

  3. It cannot exceed the state share received. The 2014 text excluded First Tranche Petroleum (FTP), the slice of production taken before cost recovery; from 2019 FTP counts unless the contract excludes it, and the contract prevails where it differs.

This page has not read PMK 139/2024, so whether these limits still apply is not confirmed. Reimbursement also depends on production. In exploration there is no state share to pay from, and PMK 122/PMK.03/2019 leaves VAT on petroleum operations uncollected ("tidak dipungut"), which keeps exploration VAT out of the receivable. Gross split contracts pay income tax under the income tax law (Note 2b, Daftar 5/17, PDF p. 34), and whether reimbursement applies to them was not verified. PHE's label is "PPN yang dapat ditagihkan kembali". Other PSC balances with the government belong to the Due from the Government essay.

For example (illustration), a PHE subsidiary in a cost-recovery PSC buys 2,000 of well services, as in section 4, and 300 of catering for a site office, VAT 33. SKK Migas accepts the first and rejects the second as not chargeable to operating costs.

Purchases (as collector): Dr Production expenses 2,000, Dr General and administrative expenses 300, Dr Reimbursable VAT 253 / Cr Trade payables 2,300, Cr VAT collected, payable 253

Claim rejected: Dr General and administrative expenses 33 / Cr Reimbursable VAT 33

Reimbursement received: Dr Cash 220 / Cr Reimbursable VAT 220

The rejected 33 is non-creditable VAT, so it becomes cost. The accepted 220 is a receivable because the PSC and the PMK give the operator a right to cash.

6. Withholding taxes: the agent's liability

Kieso's chapter lists payroll deductions among current liabilities. The employer subtracts the employee's income tax and social security contributions from gross pay and holds them until it pays them over. Indonesian law extends the role beyond payroll. A payer withholds income tax (PPh) under article 21 from employees' pay, article 23 from domestic suppliers of services, interest, dividends and royalties, article 26 from non-residents, and article 4(2) as a final tax on items such as land and building rent and construction. Since 2025 the withheld tax is due by the 15th of the following month (PMK 81/2024, art. 94).

Payroll. For example (illustration), a subsidiary's monthly payroll is 10,000 gross; it withholds PPh 21 of 1,500 and employees' social security contributions of 300.

Net pay = 10,000 − 1,500 − 300 = 8,200

Dr Salaries and wages expense 10,000 / Cr PPh 21 payable 1,500, Cr Social security contributions payable 300, Cr Salaries and wages payable 8,200

The lecture notes' version of this entry debits salaries and wages payable. The debit is the expense, because the whole 10,000 is the cost of the month's work. The employer's own contributions are a further expense and a separate liability, covered in the Employee Benefits essay.

Suppliers. For example (illustration), the subsidiary, a VAT collector, pays a consultant 500 for technical services, with PPh 23 at 2 percent and VAT at 11 percent.

PPh 23 = 500 × 2% = 10; VAT = 500 × 11% = 55; cash to the consultant = 500 + 55 − 10 − 55 = 490

Invoice: Dr Consultancy expense 500, Dr Reimbursable VAT 55 / Cr Trade payables 555

Payment: Dr Trade payables 555 / Cr PPh 23 payable 10, Cr VAT collected, payable 55, Cr Cash 490

Who bears it decides the cost. A withholding tax is the payee's tax unless the contract shifts it. For example (illustration), a non-resident engineering firm agrees to a fee of 800 "net of Indonesian tax", with PPh 26 at 20 percent and no treaty relief. The payer must gross up the fee.

Gross fee = 800 / (1 − 20%) = 1,000; PPh 26 = 1,000 × 20% = 200

Dr Engineering services expense 1,000 / Cr PPh 26 payable 200, Cr Cash 800

VAT self-assessed on the imported service = 1,000 × 11% = 110: Dr Reimbursable VAT 110 / Cr VAT on foreign services payable 110

The 200 is the payer's cost, though legally it remains the payee's tax. The 110 arises because a business that uses services from abroad pays the VAT itself (UU PPN art. 4(1)(e)); for a PSC contractor it becomes reimbursable VAT.

7. Disputes, collection letters and levies

The measurement rule for disputed income tax, ISAK 123 (formerly ISAK 34, IFRIC 23), does not reach other taxes, and Kieso's chapter would treat a possible refund as a contingent asset under PSAK 237 (formerly PSAK 57, IAS 37). The IFRS Interpretations Committee closed that route in January 2019. A payment on a disputed tax other than income tax is an asset, because the entity has a right to a refund if it wins or the payment settles the liability if it loses (see the Corporate and Dividend Taxes Receivable essay). PSAK sets no measurement rule for it; PHE carries such claims net of a provision for impairment.

For example (illustration), take a real case as the starting point. PHE's subsidiary PEP received an underpayment assessment (SKPKB) in 2015 for PPh 23 of 2011 of Rp140,606 million, about 9,136, and contested it to the Supreme Court, which rejected its judicial review on 3 December 2024 (Note 52b, Daftar 5/236–5/237, PDF pp. 253–254). PHE does not say whether PEP paid. Suppose it paid before objecting.

2015 payment: Dr Other taxes receivable, tax on assessment 9,136 / Cr Cash 9,136

Had it won: Dr Cash 9,136 / Cr Other taxes receivable 9,136, plus interest compensation (imbalan bunga) as income once virtually certain

Lost: Dr Withholding tax expense 9,136 / Cr Other taxes receivable 9,136

Paying first removes the base for the fine on tax still unpaid when an objection or appeal fails, 30 or 60 percent (UU KUP arts. 25(9) and 27(5d), as amended by UU HPP). A company that judges part way through that it will probably lose writes the receivable down to a provision before the decision. A decision given before the reporting date, even if notified after it, confirms a condition at that date and is an adjusting event (PSAK 210, formerly PSAK 8, IAS 10). The loss belongs in 2024.

A tax collection letter (Surat Tagihan Pajak, STP) for interest or penalties is challenged by a request to cancel and then a lawsuit (gugatan), as PHE ONWJ did for VAT of 2020 and 2022 (Note 43g, Daftar 5/157–5/160, PDF pp. 174–177).

Levies. PBB cannot be recovered, so it is a cost, and the question is when the liability arises. ISAK 121 Levies (formerly ISAK 30, IFRIC 21) answers that it arises at the activity that triggers the levy under the law, all at once if the trigger is a single date and progressively if it runs over time. The PBB law taxes an object according to its state on 1 January (UU 12/1985 art. 8(2)). For example (illustration), with an annual PBB of 1,200, a quarterly report shows the full 1,200 as an expense in the first quarter and none in the next three, not 300 a quarter. PHE ONWJ disputes PBB assessments for 2017–2020, for example Rp134,090 million of tax and penalties, about 8,600, for 2020 (Note 43g, Daftar 5/157, PDF p. 174).

8. Presentation: current or non-current, gross or net

Current or non-current. An asset is current when the entity expects to realise it within twelve months (PSAK 201.66, formerly PSAK 1, IAS 1). For reimbursable VAT that depends on verification time, contested items and whether the block's state share can pay the claim. For example (illustration), a subsidiary in early production holds verified claims of 120, and its block's state share over 2025 is expected to be 45.

Current = 45; non-current = 120 − 45 = 75

Dr Reimbursable VAT, non-current 75 / Cr Reimbursable VAT, current 75

No standard settles whether the non-current part is discounted, and PHE does not say.

Gross or net. PSAK 201 prohibits offsetting assets and liabilities unless a standard requires or permits it (para. 32). The VAT a contractor has collected is owed to DJP, while its reimbursable VAT is claimed through SKK Migas, so the two are shown gross even when they arise from the same purchase (section 5). Two subsidiaries' balances are not offset either, because neither has a right to settle net.

9. Other taxes across industries

Exporters. Exports carry 0 percent VAT, so output VAT is nil and input VAT is overpaid every month. Exporters may claim every month (art. 9(4b)), and low-risk taxpayers can receive a preliminary refund before examination (art. 9(4c); the implementing rule was replaced by PMK 28/2026 in May 2026). VAT receivable is a standing current asset.

Coal after 2020. Before the Job Creation Law, coal was outside VAT, so a coal miner was in section 4's position and its input VAT was cost. From 2 November 2020 coal became taxable, and unlike crude oil and piped gas (section 5) its supply was not exempted. For example (illustration), a miner buys 10,000 of mining services, VAT 1,100.

Before November 2020: Dr Mining costs 11,100 / Cr Trade payables 11,100

After: Dr Mining costs 10,000, Dr VAT input 1,100 / Cr Trade payables 11,100

The change cut the miner's production cost by 1,100 per 10,000 of purchases, and a coal exporter became a refund claimant.

Banks and insurers. Most financial services are not subject to VAT, so a bank's input VAT on rent, IT and consultants is operating expense, and its other-tax balances are mainly final tax withheld on depositors' interest.

10. Presentation and analysis: PHE's Note 43a and 43b

Note 43a gives the composition (Daftar 5/151, PDF p. 168).

Reimbursable VAT / total = 505,861 / 563,451 = 89.8% (2024); 463,608 / 489,104 = 94.8% (2023)

Non-current / total = 262,713 / 563,451 = 46.6% (2024); 213,492 / 489,104 = 43.6% (2023)

Provision / gross = 10,555 / 574,006 = 1.84% (2024)

Almost the whole line is reimbursable VAT. The subsidiaries' 475,338 is where section 5's mechanism can apply, since they hold and operate the PSCs (Note 1a, Daftar 5/1–5/2, PDF pp. 18–19). The Company's 30,523 sits at holding level, where no PSC is operated, so it may be an ordinary refund claim on its own supplies; PHE does not say. Nearly half the line is non-current, and PHE gives no reason or split by block. Possible causes are verification time at SKK Migas and the Ministry of Finance, contested items, and blocks whose state share is too small to pay their claims. The "other" category rose by 30,181 to 47,312 without explanation, and its English label, "Other prepaid taxes", says something different from the Indonesian "Piutang pajak lainnya".

Note 43b gives the payable side (Daftar 5/152, PDF p. 169).

The VAT payable is presumably mostly VAT collected from suppliers under section 4 and not yet paid over, shown gross beside the reimbursable VAT (section 8). The Company's negative PPh 4(2) payable, 84 (87 in 2023), is tax paid over in excess of tax withheld, a receivable left inside liabilities The amount is trivial, but the presentation is the kind of offsetting para. 32 prohibits.

Three further points do not reconcile.

  • The provision is 10,555 in both years, yet Note 38 shows "Impairment and correction of tax receivables" as a credit of 30,803 in 2023 and nil in 2024 (Daftar 5/149, PDF p. 166). The 2023 credit either did not pass through this provision or relates to income tax receivables.

  • Note 43g lists PEP's PPh 23 for 2011 as awaiting the judicial review decision (Daftar 5/168, PDF p. 185), while Note 52b says the Supreme Court rejected it on 3 December 2024 (section 7). The amounts for PEP's 2019 VAT assessments also differ between the two notes, and the provision did not move.

  • In Note 43g, PHE ONWJ is said to have applied on 21 February 2023 to cancel VAT collection letters that it received in November and December 2023 (Daftar 5/160, PDF p. 177).

11. Related lines

  • other-taxes-receivable-non-current: the part of the same claims expected after twelve months, covered on this page.

  • other-taxes-payable: VAT collected and taxes withheld, covered on this page.

  • corporate-dividend-taxes-receivable-current: income tax overpayments, under PSAK 212.

  • due-from-government: other PSC balances with the government.

  • production-expenses: where non-creditable or rejected VAT ends up.

  • trade-payables: the purchases that generate input VAT and withholding.

Least-confident assertions

  • The reimbursement rule in force at PHE's year end is PMK 139/2024, effective 31 December 2024, which was not read. The limits given are from the 2014 text (read in full) and a news summary of the 2019 text. Whether the right still rests with the operator, and how the cap now treats FTP, is not confirmed.

  • That PHE's reimbursable VAT arises under these PMKs is inferred from the label. PHE's VAT policy (Note 3s, Indonesian text) expenses VAT that cannot be credited and does not mention reimbursement, so as written it does not explain the 505,861. The Company's 30,523 may be an ordinary refund claim.

  • Why 46.6 percent of the line is non-current is not disclosed. The causes listed in section 10 are possibilities, not findings.

  • The exemption of crude oil, piped gas and geothermal steam was read in PP 49/2022 art. 6(2) on an OCR'd copy (pasal.id); the item letters were not checked against the official PDF.

  • No standard sets the measurement of a non-income tax receivable. Carrying it at the amount expected to be recovered, with a provision, follows PHE's practice and the 2019 agenda decision by analogy. Whether PEP paid the 2011 PPh 23 assessment, and so whether a receivable of 9,136 existed to write off, is not disclosed.

content.text: Taxes other than income tax fall outside PSAK 212. For each one, the accounting depends on who bears the tax. Tax the entity collects or withholds for the state is a liability. Tax it pays and can recover is a receivable. Tax it pays and cannot recover is part of the cost of what it bought.

Value added tax (VAT) is collected at every stage of a supply chain, and each business pays the state only output VAT less input VAT. When input exceeds output, the business is owed money. It carries the excess forward or claims a refund, and exporters and suppliers to VAT collectors are owed money most months.

An upstream oil and gas contractor sells crude and piped gas whose supply is exempt from VAT, so it cannot credit its input VAT. Under its production sharing contract (PSC) the government reimburses that VAT out of the state's share of production. At PHE, reimbursable VAT is 505,861 of the 563,451 other taxes receivable at the end of 2024, 475,338 of it in the subsidiaries that hold the PSCs.

PT Pertamina Hulu Energi and subsidiaries (PHE) report other taxes receivable, current portion, of 300,738 at 31 December 2024 against 275,612 a year earlier, and a non-current portion of 262,713 against 213,492, in USD thousand (PHE FS 2024, statement of financial position, Daftar 1/1, PDF p. 11; Note 43a, Daftar 5/151, PDF p. 168; "Daftar" is the printed page). The current portion is 0.99 percent of total assets and 3.74 percent of current assets (0.89 and 2.79 percent a year earlier); the two portions together, 563,451, are 1.85 percent of total assets. On the other side PHE owes other taxes of 153,068 against 152,476 (Note 43b, Daftar 5/152, PDF p. 169). This page covers all three lines.

After reading it a student should be able to say who bears each tax, record VAT and withholding from invoice to settlement, measure a disputed or reimbursable claim, and classify it between current and non-current.
All amounts are in USD thousand unless stated. Figures from PHE's statements are cited to their note. Every other number is labelled an illustration.

(formerly PSAK 46, IAS 12) covers taxes based on taxable profit, including taxes withheld on distributions to the entity (para. 2). Everything else is an "other" tax, such as VAT, taxes the entity withholds from other people's income, land and building tax (
, PBB), import duties and regional taxes. Corporate income tax receivable and payable, current and deferred, belong to the Corporate and Dividend Taxes Receivable and Deferred Tax essays.
No single standard covers other taxes. The accounting comes from asking who bears the tax, and the answer puts the entity in one of three roles.
Collector or agent: the tax belongs to someone else
VAT on its own sales; income tax withheld from employees and suppliers
a liability until it pays the state
Taxpayer who can recover the tax
input VAT creditable against output VAT; VAT reimbursed under a PSC
input VAT that cannot be credited; PBB; non-recoverable import duties
an expense, or part of an asset's cost

The third row is already written into the asset standards. Inventory cost includes taxes "other than those subsequently recoverable" from the tax authority (PSAK 202.11, formerly PSAK 14, IAS 2), and a fixed asset's cost includes non-refundable purchase taxes (PSAK 216.16(a), formerly PSAK 16, IAS 16).
2. Sales tax and VAT: the collector's liability

A state that wants to tax consumption cannot collect from millions of consumers, so it makes businesses collect for it. The lecture notes, following Kieso's chapter on current liabilities, distinguish a tax on every sale from a tax on value added only. In its usual form a
is charged once, at the retail sale to the consumer. A
is charged at every sale along the chain, and each business deducts the tax it paid on its purchases, so each pays the state tax only on the value it added.

For example (illustration), at the 2024 Indonesian VAT rate of 11 percent, a chemical maker sells to a distributor for 400, the distributor sells to a retailer for 700, and the retailer sells to a consumer for 1,000.
Distributor: output VAT = 700 × 11% = 77; input VAT 44; pays 33
Retailer: output VAT = 1,000 × 11% = 110; input VAT 77; pays 33
VAT reaches the retail sales tax's total in three payments of 11 percent of each stage's value added (400, 300 and 300). If the retailer evades, the state has still received 77 of the 110.
The retailer's entries, side by side, in the format of the lecture notes:
Dr Inventories 700, Dr VAT input 77 / Cr Cash 777
Dr Cash 1,110 / Cr Sales revenue 1,000, Cr Sales tax payable 110
Dr Cash 1,110 / Cr Sales revenue 1,000, Cr VAT output 110
Dr VAT output 110 / Cr VAT input 77, Cr VAT payable 33
Dr Sales tax payable 110 / Cr Cash 110

Revenue is 1,000 in both columns, because amounts collected for third parties, such as sales taxes, are not part of the transaction price (PSAK 115.47, formerly PSAK 72, IFRS 15). When a till records only the tax-inclusive total, revenue is backed out of it.
From 2025 the rate is 12 percent, but on a base of 11/12 of the price for non-luxury goods, so the effective rate stays 11 percent (PMK 131/2024).

, PKP) settles VAT by tax period, which in Indonesia is a month. Within each month it credits input VAT against output VAT (UU PPN art. 9). A positive balance is paid to the state. A negative one is an overpayment, and the general rule carries it forward to the next month as a credit (

) can be requested only at the end of the financial year (art. 9(4) and (4a)). Some businesses may request a refund every month (art. 9(4b)), among them exporters and those whose sales go to VAT collectors (section 4).
For example (illustration), a chemicals distributor selling to manufacturers records three months.
January: Dr VAT output 500 / Cr VAT input 380, Cr VAT payable 120
February: Dr VAT output 300, Dr VAT overpaid, carried forward 220 / Cr VAT input 520
March: Dr VAT output 450 / Cr VAT input 200, Cr VAT overpaid, carried forward 220, Cr VAT payable 30

The 220 at the end of February is a receivable, recovered by paying 220 less in March. At year end a refund request would start a tax examination (see the Corporate and Dividend Taxes Receivable essay).
4. When input VAT cannot be credited, and VAT collectors

Crediting needs output VAT to credit against. A business whose own supplies are not subject to VAT has none, so the input VAT it pays is a cost like any other part of the price (section 1, third row). PHE's policy, in its Indonesian text, puts VAT that "tidak dapat dikreditkan" (cannot be credited) into the cost of the asset or the expense, and carries the net VAT claimed for refund, or owed, as an asset or liability (Note 3s, Daftar 5/70, PDF p. 87). It does not mention reimbursement (section 10). For example (illustration), a company with only exempt supplies buys casing for 1,000 plus VAT of 110.

, VAT collectors. The supplier still charges VAT and issues a tax invoice, but the buyer withholds the VAT from its payment and pays it to the state itself. Upstream oil and gas contractors and geothermal contractors are such collectors, for purchases above Rp10 million (full amount) including tax (PMK 81/2024, arts. 298–299).

For example (illustration), a contractor buys 2,000 of well services, VAT 2,000 × 11% = 220. For simplicity the buyer books the collected VAT when the invoice arrives, although it collects it on payment.
Dr Production expenses 2,000, Dr VAT input 220 / Cr Trade payables 2,000, Cr VAT collected, payable 220
Dr Trade receivables 2,220 / Cr Revenue 2,000, Cr VAT output 220
Dr Cash 2,000, Dr VAT output 220 / Cr Trade receivables 2,220
Dr VAT collected, payable 220 / Cr Cash 220

The buyer settles the supplier's output VAT, so the supplier has nothing left to credit its own input VAT against. If it paid 130 of input VAT that month, it is overpaid by 130, and next month again, which is why art. 9(4b) lets it claim every month.
5. Upstream: VAT reimbursement under a PSC

An upstream contractor pays VAT on almost everything it buys and charges VAT on almost nothing it sells. Until March 2022, mining and drilling output taken directly from its source was outside VAT (UU PPN art. 4A(2)(a)). The Job Creation Law took coal out of that exclusion in November 2020, and the Harmonised Tax Law (UU 7/2021) deleted the exclusion altogether. Crude oil, piped natural gas and geothermal steam are now taxable goods whose supply is exempt (PP 49/2022, art. 6(2)). Input VAT on exempt supplies cannot be credited (art. 16B(3)), so under section 4's rule it would be a cost.

The PSC changes that. An operating contractor may claim reimbursement of the VAT it has paid on goods and services for its working area, where its contract provides for it. The rules were PMK 218/PMK.02/2014, replaced in August 2019 by PMK 119/PMK.02/2019, which was in turn replaced on 31 December 2024, PHE's balance-sheet date, by PMK 139/2024. The claim goes to SKK Migas, the upstream regulator, which verifies the tax payments with the Directorate General of Taxes (DJP), and the Ministry of Finance pays it from the oil and gas account at Bank Indonesia. Under the 2014 and 2019 texts, three limits decide how much comes back and when.
VAT that was exempt, VAT on LNG plant operating costs, and VAT on procurement that cannot be charged to operating costs are excluded (2014, art. 3(2)).
Reimbursement is paid only after the state's share of production from the working area has been received.

It cannot exceed the state share received. The 2014 text excluded First Tranche Petroleum (FTP), the slice of production taken before cost recovery; from 2019 FTP counts unless the contract excludes it, and the contract prevails where it differs.

This page has not read PMK 139/2024, so whether these limits still apply is not confirmed. Reimbursement also depends on production. In exploration there is no state share to pay from, and PMK 122/PMK.03/2019 leaves VAT on petroleum operations uncollected ("tidak dipungut"), which keeps exploration VAT out of the receivable. Gross split contracts pay income tax under the income tax law (Note 2b, Daftar 5/17, PDF p. 34), and whether reimbursement applies to them was not verified. PHE's label is "PPN yang dapat ditagihkan kembali". Other PSC balances with the government belong to the Due from the Government essay.

For example (illustration), a PHE subsidiary in a cost-recovery PSC buys 2,000 of well services, as in section 4, and 300 of catering for a site office, VAT 33. SKK Migas accepts the first and rejects the second as not chargeable to operating costs.
Purchases (as collector): Dr Production expenses 2,000, Dr General and administrative expenses 300, Dr Reimbursable VAT 253 / Cr Trade payables 2,300, Cr VAT collected, payable 253
Claim rejected: Dr General and administrative expenses 33 / Cr Reimbursable VAT 33
Reimbursement received: Dr Cash 220 / Cr Reimbursable VAT 220
The rejected 33 is non-creditable VAT, so it becomes cost. The accepted 220 is a receivable because the PSC and the PMK give the operator a right to cash.

among current liabilities. The employer subtracts the employee's income tax and social security contributions from gross pay and holds them until it pays them over. Indonesian law extends the role beyond payroll. A payer withholds income tax (PPh) under article 21 from employees' pay, article 23 from domestic suppliers of services, interest, dividends and royalties, article 26 from non-residents, and article 4(2) as a final tax on items such as land and building rent and construction. Since 2025 the withheld tax is due by the 15th of the following month (PMK 81/2024, art. 94).
For example (illustration), a subsidiary's monthly payroll is 10,000 gross; it withholds PPh 21 of 1,500 and employees' social security contributions of 300.
Dr Salaries and wages expense 10,000 / Cr PPh 21 payable 1,500, Cr Social security contributions payable 300, Cr Salaries and wages payable 8,200

The lecture notes' version of this entry debits salaries and wages payable. The debit is the expense, because the whole 10,000 is the cost of the month's work. The employer's own contributions are a further expense and a separate liability, covered in the Employee Benefits essay.
For example (illustration), the subsidiary, a VAT collector, pays a consultant 500 for technical services, with PPh 23 at 2 percent and VAT at 11 percent.
Invoice: Dr Consultancy expense 500, Dr Reimbursable VAT 55 / Cr Trade payables 555
Payment: Dr Trade payables 555 / Cr PPh 23 payable 10, Cr VAT collected, payable 55, Cr Cash 490
Who bears it decides the cost.

A withholding tax is the payee's tax unless the contract shifts it. For example (illustration), a non-resident engineering firm agrees to a fee of 800 "net of Indonesian tax", with PPh 26 at 20 percent and no treaty relief. The payer must gross up the fee.
Dr Engineering services expense 1,000 / Cr PPh 26 payable 200, Cr Cash 800
VAT self-assessed on the imported service = 1,000 × 11% = 110: Dr Reimbursable VAT 110 / Cr VAT on foreign services payable 110

The 200 is the payer's cost, though legally it remains the payee's tax. The 110 arises because a business that uses services from abroad pays the VAT itself (UU PPN art. 4(1)(e)); for a PSC contractor it becomes reimbursable VAT.

The measurement rule for disputed income tax, ISAK 123 (formerly ISAK 34, IFRIC 23), does not reach other taxes, and Kieso's chapter would treat a possible refund as a contingent asset under PSAK 237 (formerly PSAK 57, IAS 37). The IFRS Interpretations Committee closed that route in January 2019. A payment on a disputed tax other than income tax is an asset, because the entity has a right to a refund if it wins or the payment settles the liability if it loses (see the Corporate and Dividend Taxes Receivable essay). PSAK sets no measurement rule for it; PHE carries such claims net of a provision for impairment.

For example (illustration), take a real case as the starting point. PHE's subsidiary PEP received an underpayment assessment (SKPKB) in 2015 for PPh 23 of 2011 of Rp140,606 million, about 9,136, and contested it to the Supreme Court, which rejected its judicial review on 3 December 2024 (Note 52b, Daftar 5/236–5/237, PDF pp. 253–254). PHE does not say whether PEP paid. Suppose it paid before objecting.
2015 payment: Dr Other taxes receivable, tax on assessment 9,136 / Cr Cash 9,136
Had it won: Dr Cash 9,136 / Cr Other taxes receivable 9,136, plus interest compensation (
Lost: Dr Withholding tax expense 9,136 / Cr Other taxes receivable 9,136

Paying first removes the base for the fine on tax still unpaid when an objection or appeal fails, 30 or 60 percent (UU KUP arts. 25(9) and 27(5d), as amended by UU HPP). A company that judges part way through that it will probably lose writes the receivable down to a provision before the decision. A decision given before the reporting date, even if notified after it, confirms a condition at that date and is an adjusting event (PSAK 210, formerly PSAK 8, IAS 10). The loss belongs in 2024.
(Surat Tagihan Pajak, STP) for interest or penalties is challenged by a request to cancel and then a lawsuit (
), as PHE ONWJ did for VAT of 2020 and 2022 (Note 43g, Daftar 5/157–5/160, PDF pp. 174–177).
PBB cannot be recovered, so it is a cost, and the question is when the liability arises. ISAK 121

(formerly ISAK 30, IFRIC 21) answers that it arises at the activity that triggers the levy under the law, all at once if the trigger is a single date and progressively if it runs over time. The PBB law taxes an object according to its state on 1 January (UU 12/1985 art. 8(2)). For example (illustration), with an annual PBB of 1,200, a quarterly report shows the full 1,200 as an expense in the first quarter and none in the next three, not 300 a quarter. PHE ONWJ disputes PBB assessments for 2017–2020, for example Rp134,090 million of tax and penalties, about 8,600, for 2020 (Note 43g, Daftar 5/157, PDF p. 174).
8. Presentation: current or non-current, gross or net

An asset is current when the entity expects to realise it within twelve months (PSAK 201.66, formerly PSAK 1, IAS 1). For reimbursable VAT that depends on verification time, contested items and whether the block's state share can pay the claim. For example (illustration), a subsidiary in early production holds verified claims of 120, and its block's state share over 2025 is expected to be 45.
Dr Reimbursable VAT, non-current 75 / Cr Reimbursable VAT, current 75
No standard settles whether the non-current part is discounted, and PHE does not say.

PSAK 201 prohibits offsetting assets and liabilities unless a standard requires or permits it (para. 32). The VAT a contractor has collected is owed to DJP, while its reimbursable VAT is claimed through SKK Migas, so the two are shown gross even when they arise from the same purchase (section 5). Two subsidiaries' balances are not offset either, because neither has a right to settle net.

Exports carry 0 percent VAT, so output VAT is nil and input VAT is overpaid every month. Exporters may claim every month (art. 9(4b)), and low-risk taxpayers can receive a preliminary refund before examination (art. 9(4c); the implementing rule was replaced by PMK 28/2026 in May 2026). VAT receivable is a standing current asset.

Before the Job Creation Law, coal was outside VAT, so a coal miner was in section 4's position and its input VAT was cost. From 2 November 2020 coal became taxable, and unlike crude oil and piped gas (section 5) its supply was not exempted. For example (illustration), a miner buys 10,000 of mining services, VAT 1,100.
Before November 2020: Dr Mining costs 11,100 / Cr Trade payables 11,100
After: Dr Mining costs 10,000, Dr VAT input 1,100 / Cr Trade payables 11,100
The change cut the miner's production cost by 1,100 per 10,000 of purchases, and a coal exporter became a refund claimant.

Most financial services are not subject to VAT, so a bank's input VAT on rent, IT and consultants is operating expense, and its other-tax balances are mainly final tax withheld on depositors' interest.
10. Presentation and analysis: PHE's Note 43a and 43b
Note 43a gives the composition (Daftar 5/151, PDF p. 168).
Subsidiaries: withholding taxes and VAT due to tax assessments
Less provision for impairment of tax receivable

Almost the whole line is reimbursable VAT. The subsidiaries' 475,338 is where section 5's mechanism can apply, since they hold and operate the PSCs (Note 1a, Daftar 5/1–5/2, PDF pp. 18–19). The Company's 30,523 sits at holding level, where no PSC is operated, so it may be an ordinary refund claim on its own supplies; PHE does not say. Nearly half the line is non-current, and PHE gives no reason or split by block. Possible causes are verification time at SKK Migas and the Ministry of Finance, contested items, and blocks whose state share is too small to pay their claims. The "other" category rose by 30,181 to 47,312 without explanation, and its English label, "Other prepaid taxes", says something different from the Indonesian "Piutang pajak lainnya".
Note 43b gives the payable side (Daftar 5/152, PDF p. 169).

PPh 15 is a deemed-profit tax on shipping and air charter income; PPh 22 is collected on imports and certain purchases. The VAT payable is presumably mostly VAT collected from suppliers under section 4 and not yet paid over, shown gross beside the reimbursable VAT (section 8). The Company's negative PPh 4(2) payable, 84 (87 in 2023), is tax paid over in excess of tax withheld, a receivable left inside liabilities The amount is trivial, but the presentation is the kind of offsetting para. 32 prohibits.
Three further points do not reconcile.

The provision is 10,555 in both years, yet Note 38 shows "Impairment and correction of tax receivables" as a credit of 30,803 in 2023 and nil in 2024 (Daftar 5/149, PDF p. 166). The 2023 credit either did not pass through this provision or relates to income tax receivables.

In Note 43g, PHE ONWJ is said to have applied on 21 February 2023 to cancel VAT collection letters that it received in November and December 2023 (Daftar 5/160, PDF p. 177).
