For make-up gas the buyer is not expected to take, revenue follows the pattern of make-up takes and expiry.

Corrected, HEN's allowance is 826.81, and three ratios show what the face cannot

HEN's trade receivables at 31 December 2024 are 92,019.84 gross, less an allowance of 826.81. They are presented as 85,529.52 current and 5,663.51 non-current.

Gross, current = 38,000 + 45,000 + 3,240.74 = 86,240.74

Net, current = 86,240.74 − 637.20 − 9.21 − 64.81 = 85,529.52

Net, non-current = 5,779.10 − 115.59 = 5,663.51

The CFO's answers to the auditor are an affiliate allowance of 9.21 instead of 420.00, a forward-looking adjustment of 106.20, and a settlement receivable of 9,019.84 that cuts revenue by 2,980.16 and puts 5,779.10 gross in non-current.

A reader of the notes to the financial statements tests receivable quality with three ratios. The first is the allowance as a share of gross: 1.68 percent for third parties (637.20 / 38,000), 0.02 percent for related parties (9.21 / 45,000), and 0.90 percent overall (826.81 / 92,019.84). The second is days sales outstanding (DSO), the year-end gross balance divided by the year's revenue and multiplied by 365. With constructed 2024 revenue of 400,000 from crude sales to the affiliate and 260,000 from gas sales to third parties, related-party DSO is 41.1 days (45,000 / 400,000 × 365) and third-party DSO 53.3 days (38,000 / 260,000 × 365), both above 30-day terms. The third is the allowance movement, opening 900.00, write-offs 400.00, impairment loss 326.81 and closing 826.81. An allowance that falls while DSO lengthens would deserve a question.

Only notes that disclose gross balances by counterparty, the ageing, the allowance movement and the terms of anything due beyond twelve months can separate more sales from slower collection, or from an allowance set on the wrong grouping.

  • Treating the whole 2,980.16 as a reduction of revenue under PSAK 115 is the essay's reading. content.text: A trade receivable is a right to cash for crude or gas already delivered. It starts at the transaction price, sits at amortised cost, and is reduced by an allowance for lifetime expected credit losses from the day it is recognised.

The allowance depends on how customers are grouped. In the case below, applying the industrial buyers' loss rates to a state-linked affiliate would give an allowance of 420; a rate built from the affiliate's own default risk gives 9.21. The related-party label is a disclosure requirement and changes neither figure.

Cash due beyond normal terms carries a financing component. A disputed gas invoice of 12,000 settled by three annual instalments of 3,500 is worth 9,019.84 discounted at 8 percent a year, and 5,779.10 of that is non-current.
The reported line rose 6.8 percent while total assets fell, and the page cannot show how much of it is collectable

The balance sheet on this page reports trade receivables, net, of 2,203,018 at 31 December 2024 against 2,063,070 a year earlier, in thousands. That is a rise of 139,948, or 6.8 percent, in a year when total assets fell 2.9 percent. The line is 7.3 percent of total assets at 31 December 2024 (2,203,018 / 30,303,898), against 6.6 percent a year earlier. A separate line, trade receivables, net, non-current, holds 544,278 (2023: 522,121), so 19.8 percent of all trade receivables (544,278 / 2,747,296) are not expected in cash within twelve months.

Two further lines, "Third parties" at 520,885 (2023: 715,327) and "Related parties" at 823,348 (2023: 801,429), sit beside trade receivables. They total 1,344,233, not 2,203,018, so they are not its breakdown. Their labels were garbled by OCR, and they may be other receivables split by counterparty. The page cannot tell which. Either way, related-party balances are 1.58 times the third-party ones (2023: 1.12 times), and they grew 2.7 percent while third-party balances fell 27.2 percent. An upstream group often sells crude and gas to a state-owned or affiliated offtaker (the buyer that takes the production), such as a refining affiliate or the state gas company, so a related-party balance of this size is common.

This essay uses PT Hulu Energi Nusantara ("HEN"), an upstream oil and gas contractor operating under production sharing contracts (PSCs) with SKK Migas, reporting in USD under Indonesian SAK with a 31 December year end. HEN and every figure attached to it are constructed for illustration. HEN amounts are in USD thousand, except per-barrel prices in USD. HEN's parent is a state-owned energy holding. HEN sells its crude to PT Kilang Nusantara, a refining affiliate owned by the same parent, and its gas to industrial buyers and a distributor outside the group (all constructed).

At 31 December 2024 HEN's draft applies one provision matrix to all customers, and the external auditor has sent the CFO three questions. Why does the allowance treat 45,000 owed by the affiliate, of which 5,000 is 31 to 90 days past due, like a balance owed by an industrial gas buyer? Has the matrix been adjusted for conditions expected in 2025? And how should a disputed gas invoice of 12,000, settled on 31 December 2024 for three annual instalments, be measured and split between current and non-current?

The governing claim of this essay is that a trade receivable is measured as the cash HEN expects to collect, so its net figure depends on two judgments, the loss rate assigned to each group of customers and the discount applied to cash that arrives beyond normal terms. The related-party label decides what is disclosed and leaves the measurement unchanged.

This is a mechanism essay. Its verdict is that the reported line can be read only with three figures from the notes to the financial statements, the allowance as a share of gross by counterparty group, days sales outstanding by group, and the movement in the allowance, because in HEN's case the grouping alone moves the allowance by 410.79 and the discount moves 1,480.16 of revenue into interest income.

The governing standards are PSAK 115 (formerly PSAK 72, IFRS 15) for revenue, PSAK 109 (formerly 71, IFRS 9) for measurement and credit losses, PSAK 107 (formerly 60, IFRS 7) for credit-risk disclosures, PSAK 224 (formerly 7, IAS 24) for related parties, and PSAK 201 (formerly 1, IAS 1) for the current/non-current split.
A receivable starts at the transaction price, because a sale on 30-day terms has nothing to discount

A trade receivable arises when HEN has delivered and its right to payment depends only on time passing. PSAK 115 sets revenue at the transaction price, the consideration HEN expects to be entitled to. PSAK 109 then measures a trade receivable without a significant financing component (a gap between delivery and payment long enough to give one party a significant benefit of financing, whether or not interest is stated) at that same transaction price. PSAK 115 lets a seller ignore financing when the gap is expected at contract inception to be one year or less.

In December 2024 HEN lifted 480,000 barrels of its entitlement crude from PSC East and sold them to Kilang Nusantara at USD 76 per barrel, payable in 30 days. The invoice is part of the 40,000 not yet due from Kilang Nusantara at the year end.

The receivable is then held at amortised cost, because HEN's business model is to collect it and its cash flows are solely principal (and, for longer receivables, interest). For a 30-day invoice, amortised cost is the invoice less cash received and less the allowance for credit losses. That allowance is the "net" in the line's name.
Under PSAK 109 the allowance covers lifetime losses from day one, estimated through a provision matrix

PSAK 109 replaced the old incurred-loss model, under which a receivable was impaired only after a loss event such as a missed payment, with expected credit losses (ECL), the probability-weighted shortfall in cash over the receivable's life. For trade receivables without a significant financing component the standard requires the simplified approach, which means lifetime ECL from initial recognition, with no tracking of whether credit risk has increased. For trade receivables with a financing component, the simplified approach is a policy choice.

A provision matrix is the usual way to apply it. Receivables are grouped by shared credit risk, each group's balances are aged by days past due, and each bucket gets a loss rate drawn from history and adjusted for forward-looking information, conditions expected over the receivables' life that history does not reflect.

HEN's third-party receivables on normal terms are owed by industrial gas buyers in ceramics, glass and fertiliser, and five years of loss history give the historical rates below. At 31 December 2024 HEN's credit committee had a sector forecast, published in November 2024, that output in those industries would contract in 2025. Lower output cuts the buyers' sales and margins and so their capacity to pay. In the last contraction, in 2020, HEN's loss rates ran about a fifth above their five-year average, so the committee raised every rate by a fifth.
The related-party offtaker still needs an allowance, but at a rate built from its own default risk

A related party's receivable is a financial asset like any other, so PSAK 109 requires an allowance for it. The matrix groups receivables by shared credit risk characteristics, and Kilang Nusantara shares none of the industrial buyers' history. Applied anyway, HEN's matrix would give it an allowance of 420.00.

The alternative builds the rate from the affiliate's probability of default (PD) and the loss given default (LGD), the share of the balance lost if it defaults, over the time the balance is expected to stay outstanding. Kilang Nusantara's parent is state-owned and rated investment grade (BBB− or better), and the refinery is strategic to domestic fuel supply, so HEN estimates a one-year PD of 0.4 percent and an LGD of 40 percent (both constructed). The 5,000 past due is held up because the affiliate is itself waiting for compensation payments from the government, and HEN expects it within six months. HEN keeps the PD at 0.4 percent because the delay traces to the government's payment chain, not to the affiliate's own finances. If the balance reached 90 days past due, PSAK 109's rebuttable presumption of default would force a review.

The gap between 420.00 and 9.21 is the answer to the auditor's first question, and it rests on the parent's credit, not on the relationship. If the state's support for the refinery weakened, the PD would rise and so would the allowance. Past-due status still matters, because it lengthens the period over which default can occur, which is why the 5,000 carries 3.95 against 0.66 had it been current (5,000 × 0.4% × 30/365 × 40%).

PSAK 224 adds disclosure and nothing else. The full package covers the relationship, transactions, balances, terms, allowances and bad-debt expense. PSAK 224 (paragraphs 25–26) lets entities controlled by the same government give reduced disclosure, and that covers Kilang Nusantara as a sister company. Individually significant transactions, such as HEN's crude sales to the affiliate, must still be disclosed by nature and amount. In such a group "related parties" may reach every state-owned company, so the page's two counterparty lines say nothing about risk.
Cash due beyond twelve months carries a financing component, so the receivable is discounted and its interest unwinds

When payment falls due much later than delivery, part of the consideration is interest, and PSAK 115 removes it from revenue. The discount rate is the rate the parties would use in a separate financing transaction, which reflects the customer's credit risk. The owner's notes teach this with a crude cargo sold for a four-year non-interest-bearing note, recognised at present value with the difference earned as interest each year.

HEN's case is a gas dispute. In November and December 2023 HEN invoiced 12,000 of price escalation under a gas sales contract with PT Gas Distribusi Barat, a third-party distributor. The buyer had not objected by 29 February 2024, when HEN's 2023 statements were issued, so HEN recognised the revenue in 2023. In March 2024 the buyer disputed the escalation index and withheld payment. On 31 December 2024 the parties settled at 10,500, payable in three instalments of 3,500 on 31 December 2025, 2026 and 2027, with no interest. Gas Distribusi Barat would pay 8 percent a year on a three-year unsecured loan (constructed).

Because the dispute concerned the price HEN was entitled to, not the buyer's ability to pay, this essay treats both amounts as a change in the transaction price of the 2023 sales, recognised as a reduction of 2024 revenue. Practice is divided. The IASB's April 2024 post-implementation review of IFRS 15 recorded that some entities treat a price reduction as a price concession under IFRS 15 and others as an expected credit loss under IFRS 9.
Dr Trade receivables, settlement (at present value) 9,019.84
Cr Trade receivables, third parties (disputed invoices) 12,000.00

The current/non-current boundary runs through this receivable. HEN splits it by the present value of each instalment, so the current portion is the present value of the 2025 instalment. Some preparers instead classify as current the 2,778.41 by which the carrying amount falls in 2025 (3,500 less 721.59 of interest), leaving 6,241.43 non-current. PSAK 201 prescribes neither, and HEN's policy uses the first.
Interest unwinds at 8 percent a year on the opening carrying amount.
Dr Trade receivables, settlement 721.59 / Cr Interest income 721.59 (31 Dec 2025)
Dr Cash 3,500.00 / Cr Trade receivables, settlement 3,500.00 (31 Dec 2025)

At 31 December 2025 the 6,241.43 splits again, 3,240.74 current and 3,000.69 non-current. HEN's policy applies the simplified approach to this receivable too, at a lifetime rate of 2 percent (constructed) for a buyer that has just agreed to pay.
Writing off a bankrupt buyer leaves profit unchanged, because the expense arose when the allowance was built

Writing off the 400 owed by an industrial gas buyer that went bankrupt in 2024, with nothing for unsecured creditors, had no effect on 2024 profit. A write-off derecognises (removes from the balance sheet) the part of a receivable HEN has no reasonable expectation of recovering, and it is booked against the allowance.
Dr Allowance for expected credit losses 400
The year's impairment loss is whatever brings the allowance to its required closing balance after write-offs. HEN's allowance opened 2024 at 900.
Dr Impairment loss on trade receivables 326.81
Cr Allowance for expected credit losses 326.81
